messages.subject: Customizing activityOverlap plots
parts:
Hello camtrapR users,

I'm plotting activity overlap of two species using the activityOverlap() function in camtrapR. I'm struggling to figure out how to issue commands to customize the plot box. Specifically, I need to remove the title ("Activity overlap: SpeciesA - Species B"), the subtitle ("number of records: # / #") and the Dhat1 text on the plot. Many other visual plotting commands seem to default to the R plot standards but main=NA and sub=NA (and other variations, e.g. NULL and "", recommended on help forums) don't seem to the do the trick.

Here's the code I'm using to make the plot; since it's the plotting commands, not the data specifically, I'm questioning, you could replace the data with anything:

activityOverlap(recordTable = data,
                speciesA = "Leopard",
                speciesB = "Lion",
                speciesCol = "Common",
                recordDateTimeCol = "DateTime",
                recordDateTimeFormat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
                plotR = TRUE,
                writePNG = FALSE,
                addLegend = TRUE,
                legendPosition = "bottomright",
                createDir = FALSE,
                pngMaxPix = 1000,
                add.rug = FALSE,
                extend = NULL,
                xaxs="i", yaxs="i", main=NA, sub=NA
               
)

Thanks in advance for your help,
Jennie Miller

messages.subject: Re: Customizing activityOverlap plots
parts:
Hi Jennie,
you are right, currently the three text items in the plot you mentioned cannot be changed.
But because the function activityOverlap is basically nothing but a convenient wrapper around the function overlapPlot from the overlap package you can also use that function instead. All you need to do is convert the time of day to radial time (which ranges from 0 to 2 pi). Then, you can use the overlapPlot function to your heart's desire. Here's a little convenience function which converts a time vector to radial time (omitting the date information). Adjust timeformat to match your data (it should work with the default output of recordTable).


ClocktimeToTimeRad <- function(Clocktime,
                               timeformat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"){

  DateTime2 <- strptime(as.character(Clocktime), format = timeformat, tz = "UTC")
  Time2     <- format(DateTime2, format = "%H:%M:%S", usetz = FALSE)
  Time.rad  <- (as.numeric(as.POSIXct(strptime(Time2, format = "%H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC"))) -
                  as.numeric(as.POSIXct(strptime("0", format = "%S", tz = "UTC")))) / 3600 * (pi/12)
  return(Time.rad)
}

Here's an example for running it with the sample data:

data("recordTableSample")
recordTableSample$TimeRad <- ClocktimeToTimeRad(recordTableSample$DateTimeOriginal)

and for generating the plot:


# choose species
speciesA <- "VTA"
speciesB <- "PBE"

# set legend parameters. You can play around with these
legendPosition <- "topleft"
legendText <- c(speciesA, speciesB)
lty.tmp <- c(1, 2)
lwd.tmp <- c(1, 1)
col.tmp <- c("black", "blue")


# do plot
overlapPlot(A = recordTableSample[recordTableSample$Species == speciesA, "TimeRad"],
            B = recordTableSample[recordTableSample$Species == speciesB, "TimeRad"],
            main = "")

# add legend
legend(x = legendPosition,
       legend = legendText,
       lty = lty.tmp,
       lwd = lwd.tmp,
       col = col.tmp,
       bg = "white"
)
